text:
## Description

Read a circular binary sequence and report whether a single uppercase English string of the same length permits operations that turn every entry into 1.

## Preconditions

- PRE-1 (Unverified). Standard input gives an integer \(N\) on the first line and \(N\) space-separated integers \(A_1,\ldots,A_N\) on the second line.
- PRE-2 (Unverified). \(3 \le N \le 200000\), and every \(A_i\) is either 0 or 1.

## Postconditions

- POST-1 (Unverified). Print `Yes` exactly when there exists one fixed string \(S\) of \(N\) uppercase English letters for which a permitted sequence of operations leaves all entries equal to 1. Otherwise print `No`.
- POST-2 (Unverified). At any start \(i\) from 1 through \(N\), the three consecutive characters of \(S\) must be `ARC` or `CRA` to permit an operation. Indices wrap around the end for both the character pattern and the sequence update.
- POST-3 (Unverified). Each operation sets only \(A_i\) and \(A_{i+1}\) to 1. Either entry may already be 1. Operations may overlap or repeat, and \(S\) remains fixed throughout. Zero operations are allowed, so an all-ones input always yields `Yes`.
- POST-4 (Unverified). Standard output contains one verdict on its own line. The judge accepts any capitalization of `Yes` or `No`.

## Test suggestions

All inputs satisfy PRE-1 and PRE-2. Expected stdout is shown as the complete output line.

- Minimum length with zero operations (POST-3, POST-4). Expected `Yes`.
  ```text
  3
  1 1 1
  ```
- The two zeros can share an operation across the boundary (POST-1, POST-2). Expected `Yes`.
  ```text
  3
  0 1 0
  ```
- One fixed string can use both pattern orientations (POST-1, POST-2). Expected `Yes`.
  ```text
  4
  0 0 0 0
  ```
- Two operations can cover four zeros while leaving an existing 1 in place (POST-1, POST-3). Expected `Yes`.
  ```text
  5
  0 0 1 0 0
  ```
- Matching a three-character pattern does not set the third entry (POST-1, POST-3). Expected `No`.
  ```text
  5
  0 0 0 0 0
  ```
- Covering six zeros with three pairs would require incompatible character assignments in the fixed circular string (POST-1, POST-2). Expected `No`.
  ```text
  6
  0 0 0 0 0 0
  ```

## Unspecified behavior

Malformed input, extra or missing values, noninteger values, and values outside the stated bounds have unspecified behavior.

Document a semi-formal behavioral contract for the supplied programming task. A separate
coding model will implement and test the program; the contract states WHAT a correct program must
output, never HOW to compute it. Use exactly these headings:
## Description
One or two sentences on the externally observable input/output behavior.
## Preconditions
PRE-1 etc: input format, value ranges and guarantees from the statement. Mark each Unverified.
## Postconditions
POST-1 etc: exact properties of a correct output, including boundary behavior, ties, ordering,
multiplicity, invariants and output format. Prefer properties that separate a correct answer from
plausible but wrong answers. Mark each Unverified.
## Test suggestions
4-6 concrete checks, each tied to PRE/POST IDs, written as a small stdin input and the exact
expected stdout that you derived by hand from the statement alone. Choose inputs that a plausible
but wrong program would answer incorrectly (beyond the statement's own samples), plus at least one
boundary input. Keep every input small enough to check by hand. Do not claim tests were run.
## Unspecified behavior
List behavior outside the task's guarantees, without inventing validation rules.
Use natural language. Do not provide code, pseudocode, algorithms, data structures or complexity
advice, and do not hint at how to compute the answer. No existing implementation or tests have been
inspected. Do not mark any condition Tested or Verified. Keep the contract within about 400 words.

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
